items.label: Placode
items.question: What does the paper say about the structure or morphology of hair placode? (hair placode is also referred to as: placode, epidermal placode, epithelial hair placode.)
items.answer: A focal thickening of the epidermal layer, formed by budding of basal cells; placode formation is accompanied by invagination as the dermal condensate forms beneath it.
items.span: epidermal placodes (focal sites of epidermal layer thickening)

items.label: Placode
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is hair placode found? (hair placode is also referred to as: placode, epidermal placode, epithelial hair placode.)
items.answer: In the epidermis, at focal sites of epidermal thickening; the dermal condensate abuts the epithelial hair placode from below.
items.span: which abuts the epithelial hair placode

items.label: Placode
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to hair placode? (hair placode is also referred to as: placode, epidermal placode, epithelial hair placode.)
items.answer: Initiates hair follicle formation together with the dermal condensate; hair matrix cells arise from the epidermal placode. WNT and EDA signalling drive placode specification.
items.span: We evaluated hair matrix cells, which arise from the epidermal placode

items.label: Placode
items.question: Which genes mark hair placode? (hair placode is also referred to as: placode, epidermal placode, epithelial hair placode.)
items.answer: LAMP1, CXADR and EPHB6 are reported on the placode, as receptors for FAM3C and EFNB1 expressed by the dermal condensate.
items.span: predicted to interact with LAMP1 or CXADR and EPHB6 on the placode
items.hazard: The genes are receptors *on* the placode named in a ligand-receptor prediction, not a marker panel. An answer naming them is correct; one calling them placode markers is over-reading.

items.label: Macrophage
items.question: Which genes mark macrophage?
items.answer: MHCII genes (upregulated only after 11 PCW), TREM2 on the microglia-like subset with P2RY12, CX3CR1 and OLFML3; GAS6 and VEGFA and CXCL8 also macrophage-expressed.
items.span: share an expression profile (P2RY12, CX3CR1 and OLFML3) with microglia-like macrophages
items.hazard: broad label; four subsets each have their own markers

items.label: Macrophage
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is macrophage found?
items.answer: Seed the skin from 6 PCW; co-locate with endothelial and neural cells in the early and late neurovascular microenvironments (ME1 and ME5), and with fibroblasts (ME1, ME4, ME5).
items.span: Macrophages co-located with endothelial and neural cells in ‘early and late neurovascular microenvironments’

items.label: Macrophage
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to macrophage?
items.answer: Support angiogenesis via vascular network remodelling, contribute to scarless skin repair, fibroblast homeostasis and neurovascular development.
items.span: Our atlas indicated that macrophages contribute to scarless skin repair, fibroblast homeostasis and neurovascular development.

items.label: WNT2+ fibroblast
items.question: Which genes mark WNT2+ fibroblast?
items.answer: WNT2 itself; late-gestation cells upregulate COL1A1 and extracellular matrix/collagen genes, early cells SFRP1; the population also expresses CDKN1A, IL1R1 and POSTN, and has downregulated IL6 relative to adult.
items.span: Late gestation WNT2+ fibroblasts had upregulated genes related to extracellular matrix and collagen deposition

items.label: WNT2+ fibroblast
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is WNT2+ fibroblast found?
items.answer: Dermal; co-locate with LYVE1+ macrophages, and with TML macrophages in early prenatal skin (6-8 PCW).
items.span: Specifically, LYVE1+ macrophages co-located with WNT2+ fibroblasts

items.label: WNT2+ fibroblast
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to WNT2+ fibroblast?
items.answer: Extracellular matrix and collagen deposition in late gestation, growth and differentiation early; acquire an adult pro-inflammatory and senescence profile with gestational age.
items.span: we observed differences within the WNT2+ fibroblast population across gestation time

items.label: TML macrophage
items.question: Which genes mark TREM2+ microglia-like (TML) macrophage? (TREM2+ microglia-like (TML) macrophage is also referred to as: TML macrophage.)
items.answer: TREM2, with P2RY12, CX3CR1 and OLFML3; also express GAS6.
items.span: Prenatal skin TREM2+ microglia-like (TML) macrophages were highly correlated with embryonic brain microglia

items.label: TML macrophage
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is TREM2+ microglia-like (TML) macrophage found? (TREM2+ microglia-like (TML) macrophage is also referred to as: TML macrophage.)
items.answer: Co-locate with WNT2+ fibroblasts in early prenatal skin (6-8 PCW) and with Schwann cells in the early neurovascular microenvironment (ME1); seen in close proximity to endothelial cells.
items.span: TML macrophages were predicted to co-locate with WNT2+ fibroblasts in early prenatal skin

items.label: TML macrophage
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to TREM2+ microglia-like (TML) macrophage? (TREM2+ microglia-like (TML) macrophage is also referred to as: TML macrophage.)
items.answer: Promote sprouting angiogenesis, and interact with Schwann cells to contribute to synapse formation and axon guidance (VEGFA-NRP1, VEGFA-NRP2, SEMA3C-NRP2, SEMA3E-PLXND1).
items.span: contributing to synapse formation and axon guidance

items.label: Dermal condensate
items.question: Which genes mark dermal condensate? (dermal condensate is also referred to as: Dc.)
items.answer: FOXD1+SOX2+ (the precursor pre-Dc is PDGFRA+FOXD1+SOX2-low); the Dc expresses FAM3C and EFNB1.
items.span: expressed FAM3C and EFNB1

items.label: Dermal condensate
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is dermal condensate found? (dermal condensate is also referred to as: Dc.)
items.answer: In the dermal compartment from 12 PCW, directly beneath and abutting the epithelial hair placode.
items.span: Within the dermal compartment, we observed HF-specialized fibroblasts, the dermal condensate (Dc) and dermal papilla (Dp), from 12 PCW

items.label: Dermal condensate
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to dermal condensate? (dermal condensate is also referred to as: Dc.)
items.answer: Aggregates from pre-Dc fibroblasts to initiate hair follicle formation with the placode; its FAM3C and EFNB1 are predicted to promote cell migration and invasion.
items.span: have been reported to promote cell migration and invasion

items.label: Matrix
items.question: Which genes mark hair matrix? (hair matrix is also referred to as: matrix, hair matrix cells, matrix cells.)
items.answer: SHH, and WNT10B; both described as known matrix markers.
items.span: known matrix markers such as SHH and WNT10B, were upregulated
items.hazard: "Matrix" alone is ambiguous in this paper -- extracellular matrix and several linear-algebra senses dominate raw matches. The question must say hair matrix.

items.label: Matrix
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is hair matrix found? (hair matrix is also referred to as: matrix, hair matrix cells, matrix cells.)
items.answer: In the hair follicle, arising from the epidermal placode; a prenatal-specific cell state absent from established adult follicles. Identified from 14 PCW.
items.span: a prenatal-specific cell state absent in established adult HFs

items.label: Matrix
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to hair matrix? (hair matrix is also referred to as: matrix, hair matrix cells, matrix cells.)
items.answer: Expresses chemotaxis genes including CXCL14, reported to recruit regulatory T cells, and CD24 in control of autoimmunity - suggesting Treg accumulation and immune protection during early matrix differentiation.
items.span: increased expression of genes involved in chemotaxis, such as CXCL14

items.label: LYVE1++ macrophage
items.question: Which genes mark LYVE1+ macrophage? (LYVE1+ macrophage is also referred to as: LYVE1++ macrophage.)
items.answer: LYVE1; also expresses GAS6.
items.span: GAS6, expressed by TML macrophages and LYVE1+ macrophages
items.hazard: The roster label writes LYVE1++, the paper writes LYVE1+. Marker evidence in the body text is thin - the subset's DEG panel is in Supplementary Table 22.

items.label: LYVE1++ macrophage
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is LYVE1+ macrophage found? (LYVE1+ macrophage is also referred to as: LYVE1++ macrophage.)
items.answer: Co-locate with WNT2+ fibroblasts in the dermis, and are seen in close proximity to endothelial cells by RNAscope and immunofluorescence.
items.span: showed LYVE1+ and TML macrophages in close proximity to endothelial cells

items.label: LYVE1++ macrophage
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to LYVE1+ macrophage? (LYVE1+ macrophage is also referred to as: LYVE1++ macrophage.)
items.answer: Promote sprouting angiogenesis and blood vessel morphogenesis, and maintain prenatal skin dermal fibroblasts (via PDGF-PDGFR and GAS6-AXL).
items.span: blood vessel morphogenesis by LYVE1+ macrophages

items.label: Fibroblast
items.question: Which genes mark fibroblast?
items.answer: Prenatal skin fibroblasts upregulate immune-suppression and regeneration genes (CD200, RAMP2, MDK) relative to adult, which express IL6, IL1RA, HLA-A, CD55, PTGES and CDKN1A. They do not significantly express papillary markers such as COL13A1.
items.span: prenatal skin fibroblasts had upregulated genes involved in immune suppression (CD200)
items.hazard: broad label spanning five fine subsets; answers may legitimately be subset-specific

items.label: Fibroblast
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is fibroblast found?
items.answer: Dermal compartment. HOXC5+ early fibroblasts sit in the upper dermis; HF-specialised subsets (Dc, Dp) are within the dermal compartment from 12 PCW.
items.span: HOXC5+ early fibroblasts (located in the upper dermis

items.label: Fibroblast
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to fibroblast?
items.answer: Early-gestation fibroblasts downregulate extracellular matrix formation, collagen deposition and inflammation, which may favour tissue regeneration over scarring.
items.span: may favour tissue regeneration over scarring

items.label: Periderm
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is periderm found?
items.answer: The outermost layer, overlying the dermal stroma in skin up to 8 PCW; present from 7 PCW, enriched in early gestation, and seen sloughing from 11 PCW.
items.span: with the periderm seen sloughing from 11 PCW

items.label: Periderm
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to periderm?
items.answer: Constitutes the first skin permeability barrier.
items.span: the periderm, which constitutes the first skin permeability barrier

items.label: Periderm
items.question: What does the paper say about the structure or morphology of periderm?
items.answer: A layer of epidermal cells overlying the dermal stroma, which sloughs from 11 PCW.
items.span: consisted of a layer of epidermal cells overlying the dermal stroma
items.hazard: thin - a layer description and a sloughing observation, not morphology proper

items.label: HOXC5+ early fibroblast
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is HOXC5+ early fibroblast found? (HOXC5+ early fibroblast is also referred to as: HOXC5+ fibroblast.)
items.answer: The upper dermis.
items.span: HOXC5+ early fibroblasts (located in the upper dermis

items.label: HOXC5+ early fibroblast
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to HOXC5+ early fibroblast? (HOXC5+ early fibroblast is also referred to as: HOXC5+ fibroblast.)
items.answer: A common fibroblast progenitor: differentiates along a hair fibroblast trajectory (pre-Dc, Dc, Dp) and a dermal fibroblast trajectory (WNT2+ and PEAR1+ fibroblasts).
items.span: originated from a common fibroblast progenitor (HOXC5+ early fibroblast)

items.label: DPYSL2+ basal
items.question: Which genes mark DPYSL2+ basal cell? (DPYSL2+ basal cell is also referred to as: DPYSL2+ basal, mature basal.)
items.answer: DPYSL2 itself, and AGR2 - reported as newly identified along the ORS/CL trajectory. BARX2 and SOX9 are named in the same sentence but explicitly as previously reported ORS-differentiation genes.
items.span: we identified new genes upregulated by DPYSL2+ basal cells, such as AGR2
items.hazard: This is the rule-1 trap. An answer of "AGR2" is right; "BARX2, SOX9" is reading the paper's attribution backwards. Judge must be told the distinction, not left to infer it.

items.label: DPYSL2+ basal
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to DPYSL2+ basal cell? (DPYSL2+ basal cell is also referred to as: DPYSL2+ basal, mature basal.)
items.answer: Part of the ORS/CL differentiation trajectory from POSTN+ basal cells, towards outer root sheath and companion layer.
items.span: ORS/CL trajectory, comprising DPYSL2+ basal cells, ORS and CL

items.label: Capillary arterioles
items.question: Which genes mark capillary arteriole? (capillary arteriole is also referred to as: capillary arteriole cells.)
items.answer: Arteriolar identity is marked by GJA5. In the organoid comparison, KDR and FLT1 (VEGF receptors) and the GATA2/NFATC1 regulons with targets such as VWF are downregulated in SkO capillary arterioles relative to prenatal skin.
items.span: their receptors (KDR and FLT1) on SkO capillary arterioles were downregulated compared to prenatal skin

items.label: Capillary arterioles
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to capillary arteriole? (capillary arteriole is also referred to as: capillary arteriole cells.)
items.answer: In prenatal skin they can differentiate further into arterioles, which SkO capillary arteriole cells cannot; they score highly for the sprouting angiogenesis tip-cell state.
items.span: prenatal skin capillary arteriole cells could further differentiate into arterioles

items.label: PEAR1+ fibroblast
items.question: Which genes mark PEAR1+ fibroblast?
items.answer: PEAR1 itself; APOE, IGFBP7 and ITM2A are upregulated during the transition from HOXC5+ fibroblasts, as a pro-inflammatory fibroblast phenotype.
items.span: were also upregulated during the transition from HOXC5+ fibroblasts into PEAR1+ fibroblasts

items.label: PEAR1+ fibroblast
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to PEAR1+ fibroblast?
items.answer: A dermal fibroblast endpoint, abundant after 11 PCW, carrying the adult pro-inflammatory gene expression profile along with senescence and collagen deposition genes.
items.span: formed WNT2+ fibroblasts and PEAR1+ fibroblasts (abundant after 11 PCW)

items.label: POSTN+ basal
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is POSTN+ basal cell found? (POSTN+ basal cell is also referred to as: POSTN+ basal.)
items.answer: Basal epidermis; present throughout gestation, unlike mature DPYSL2+ basal and suprabasal IFE cells which increase after 11 PCW.
items.span: whereas POSTN+ basal cells were present throughout gestation

items.label: POSTN+ basal
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to POSTN+ basal cell? (POSTN+ basal cell is also referred to as: POSTN+ basal.)
items.answer: Increased cellular migration, suggested to be involved in placode specification and dermal invagination; the origin of both the ORS/CL and IRS differentiation trajectories.
items.span: may be involved in placode specification and dermal invagination

items.label: Arterioles
items.question: Which genes mark arteriole?
items.answer: GJA5, given as the characteristic arteriolar gene (against PLVAP for venular).
items.span: for example, GJA5 for arteriolar and PLVAP for venular
items.hazard: Shares nearly every sentence with Capillary arterioles; an answer drawn from the capillary-arteriole evidence should not be marked wrong without checking which label the sentence attributes it to.

items.label: Arterioles
items.question: What function does the paper attribute to arteriole?
items.answer: The endpoint of the arteriolar differentiation pathway from early endothelial cells via capillaries and capillary arterioles; scores for sprouting angiogenesis tip-cell state.
items.span: differentiated into either an arteriolar pathway (capillaries, capillary arterioles and arterioles)

items.label: Cuticle/cortex
items.question: Where in prenatal human skin is cuticle/cortex found? (cuticle/cortex is also referred to as: cuticle and cortex cells.)
items.answer: Part of the inner layers of the hair follicle.
items.span: part of the inner layers of the HF
